notes: Three electors pledged to Monroe, one each in Mississippi, Pennsylvania and Tennessee, died before the Electoral College met and were not replaced. As a result, 232 of the 235 electoral votes were cast.
Missouri’s statehood was disputed when the votes were counted, and Congress read the count both with and without its 3 electoral votes. They are included here, giving Monroe 231 rather than 228.

For vice president, Daniel D. Tompkins was re-elected with 218 electoral votes. Other electors gave Richard Stockton 8, Daniel Rodney 4, Robert Goodloe Harper 1 and Richard Rush 1, and 3 votes were not cast.
William Plumer, an elector from New Hampshire, voted for John Quincy Adams as a faithless elector.

The Federalists had no presidential candidate, and 14 of Monroe’s electoral votes came from Federalist electors in Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland and Massachusetts. In Massachusetts the Federalist slate won the popular vote, but its electors voted for Monroe.
The 18,719 votes for Federalist elector slates appear as “No candidate.” In Pennsylvania an anti-Monroe ticket pledged to DeWitt Clinton received 1,893 votes.

In Kentucky the one Federalist elector chosen, John Pope, was pledged to Monroe and voted for him, so his 1,941 votes are counted for Monroe. Wikipedia’s national table lists them under the Federalists.
